# framegx

> Inspect a rendered animation for black, frozen, wrong-length or sound-less output. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes a contact-sheet storyboard.

framegx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. ManimGX checks the
scene before rendering; framegx checks the rendered file — the part a scene
inspector cannot see.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/framegx" framegx --help
uv tool install ./packages/framegx      # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+ and `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` on PATH.

## Use

```sh
framegx inspect clip.py            # report + contact sheet, exit 1 on any error
framegx inspect clip.py --json
framegx inspect clip.py --no-storyboard
```

A clip file defines `video` (a `framegx.Video`) or module-level `PATH` /
`EXPECTED_DURATION` / `EXPECTED_FPS` / `EXPECTED_SIZE` / `EXPECT_AUDIO`.

```python
import framegx as f

video = f.Video("out.mp4", expected_duration=9.0, expect_audio=True)
```

## Checks

error: `missing-file`, `probe-error`, `no-frames`, `all-black`, `frozen`.
warn: `single-color`, `no-motion`, `duration-mismatch`, `wrong-fps`,
`wrong-size`, `no-audio`, `silent-audio`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
